answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may influence a shared reputation score. A velvet onboarding flow might issue an opal badge only after a juniper task is completed, but the stake is the Sybil defense: identities that behave honestly can recover it, while proven fraud triggers slashing. An attacker creating hundreds of identities must therefore immobilize substantial capital and risks losing it, rather than gaining influence at negligible cost.
